data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject only if the test's assertions are independent of the subject's declared data; when a guard checks declared data, the test describes that declaration, and the 1/9 loss is a declared-data mutation that no test asserted on because the declaration was not in the test's fixture.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the lost mutation was in executable code rather than declared data, the declaration-independence mechanism does not apply.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the ordinarily-guarded modules' tests assert on behavior derived from declarations rather than declarations themselves, the description claim is weak.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If compile.py's mutation operators include fixture mutation, the invisibility claim fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The surviving mutations in the ordinarily-guarded modules are all guard-checked declarations. The test describes the declaration because the test imports the declared data and asserts on its shape, not on the behavior that the declaration is supposed to enable. The 1/9 lost mutation under shown-to-fail-first installation is a declaration change that the test fixture did not load, so the test neither constrained nor described it \u2014 it was invisible.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
